Arnold press: starts in front (shoulder flexion, elbows forward), rotates into a frontal-plane press (abduction) to overhead. anterior_delts PRIMARY (prime mover of overhead elevation); lateral_delts SECONDARY (abduction component during the rotation-out phase). triceps SECONDARY: elbow extension is loaded but the press is credited as indirect work for the elbow extensors (synergist of the compound press, fractional counting EV-08 logic). pecs MINOR: clavicular head assists shoulder flexion only in the low range of an overhead press. upper_back MINOR: scapular upward rotation accompanies overhead elevation; treated as a supporting/stabilising contribution in a press (reviewer may argue SECONDARY). abs MINOR: trunk bracing under an overhead free weight; seated vs standing not stated, MINOR holds for both. No catalogue description; bench not listed because seated vs standing is not stated. failure_safe false: dumbbells overhead.
review: upper_back MINOR -> SECONDARY (joint_action_anatomy, EV-71). Cross-record consistency: the lateral raises credit upper_back SECONDARY for the trapezius upward-rotating the scapula under arm elevation (D.2 synergist of shoulder_abduction); an overhead press drives the same loaded upward rotation through a larger arc, so it cannot be MINOR here and SECONDARY there. Applied to all five overhead presses whatever the grip (upward rotation is obligatory in overhead flexion as in abduction); the curator had flagged it ('reviewer may argue SECONDARY').
review: reviewer claude-review-upper

Variant stated by the catalogue (hamstring bias = hinge at the hip, knees extended, spine held neutral). Loaded hip extension from deep flexion with the knee extended: biarticular hamstrings are lengthened and are the prime mover -> hamstrings PRIMARY; glute max and adductor magnus are hip-extension synergists -> SECONDARY (D.2, decided for this exercise, not copied from the legacy label). Spinal erectors carry the trunk (no zone); abs are antagonists of the gravitational trunk-flexion moment -> no role. No registry longitudinal trial. equipment_gap: 45-degree back-extension bench (roman chair). failure_safe: bodyweight on a pad, no crushing at failure (if a plate is held, it can be dropped forward safely).
